notes.text: You choose one of six specialisations from semester 1 and take its elective course (1 ECTS) in semesters 1, 3 and 6. Source: brochure (version 2026/08), “Vertiefung (Wahlpflichtfächer)”.

courses.title: Basic nursing competence
courses.content: Definition of the terms perception, cognition, consciousness; differences between cognitive and perceptive abilities; types of sensory perception; problems of people with limitations of sensory perception or disorders of consciousness. Perception of individuality, autonomy and sense of shame of clients* of all ages in nursing actions. Body care: observation and assessment of facial expressions, gestures, mood, posture, hygiene, skin and mucous membrane and of changes such as exsiccosis, cachexia, decubitus, intertrigo and contractures. Nursing Interventions: Bath, infant bath, shower, partial wash, oral, dental and denture care, hair care, shaving, nasal, ear and eye care; prophylaxis: Intertrigo, thrush and parotitis; Nutrition at all ages: Observation, assessment, methods of measurement of nutritional status and fluid balance; Nursing interventions: Assistance with feeding in impaired and dysphagic patients, fluid balance; Prophylaxis: Aspiration prophylaxis Excretion in all ages: Physiological parameters, observation and recognition of changes in excretion, forms of incontinence, prophylaxis against constipation and diarrhea, continence training; sexuality and incontinence. Sleep in all ages: physiological parameters, observation of changes in sleep behavior, stages of consciousness, preventive interventions: Sleep promotion; Posture and movement: Observation of changes in posture and movement, problems of immobility prophylaxis: prevention of thrombosis, contractures, pressure sores. Safety and prevention for all ages: Orientation in new environment, compliance, duty to inform, hygiene, self-protection; prophylaxis: fall prevention. Vital signs at all ages (body temperature, respiration, pulse and blood pressure): Physiological parameters, observation and recognition of changes in vital functions, nursing interventions: Wraps; prophylaxis: pneumonia prophylaxis. Nursing techniques: dressing materials, application techniques, dressing changes, medication management (administration methods, handling, storage). Basics of nursing documentation
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni define the terms perception and cognition and explain their meaning for people of all ages. They define the term consciousness. They describe types of sensory perception as the basis for cognitive processing. They contrast and explain self-perception and perception by others as an important competency for professional practice. Alumni understand physiological and pathological relationships in the areas of personal hygiene, nutrition, elimination, sleep, movement, perception and safety. They perceive deviations and disorders in clients of all age groups. They support clients in these areas and carry out prophylaxis. They master the skills, abilities and strategies required to carry out simple therapeutic and diagnostic measures in accordance with medical instructions. In doing so, they integrate central principles, action sequences, methods and techniques of health care and nursing after critical review situation- and individual-related into the nursing action and take into account economic and ecological criteria. Alumni elicit, interpret, and document vital signs; in the event of deviations from the norm, they forward them. Alumni demonstrate basic dressing application techniques. They are proficient in the use of materials for wound care. Alumni master the handling of medications, know the different forms of application, prepare and administer medications correctly, and perform patient*internal observation after administration. The alumni know the basics of nursing documentation. They document the nursing care provided in the implementation record and observations or deviations in the nursing report in a process-oriented manner.

courses.title: History and philosophy of nursing
courses.content: Basic knowledge of philosophical theories (e.g. Aristotle and Plato, Kant, Descartes), image of man (mechanistic, scientific-technical, holistic, humanistic, existentialist), definition of nursing understanding. History of nursing from antiquity to the present in a socio-cultural context (national and international).
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni describe the basic knowledge from history and philosophy of the profession of nursing. They reflect on the international development of nursing and compare it with the Austrian status. They discuss norms and values in a socio-cultural context and establish a relationship to the understanding of nursing. They understand health care and nursing as a human encounter and social mission.

courses.title: Internship and Skills Lab 1
courses.content: Communication with team members, patients, clients, residents, family members, other professionals. Basic nursing skills Special nursing activities (depending on the practice site) Knowledge and coordination of procedures Relevant medical, pharmacological, dietary knowledge Relevant nursing concepts Skills and simulation training
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni practice and reflect on patient situations and skills in simulations and skills training. The alumni integrate themselves into a nursing team. They communicate appropriately with colleagues, clients, patients, residents and relatives. Alumni perform basic nursing activities in the core nursing competence and in the competence in medical diagnostics and therapy under supervision and guidance. They are aware of the responsibilities involved in performing tasks and know the limits of their scope of practice. They document nursing procedures performed in an appropriate manner. They know the procedure in the practice area and help to shape it in a meaningful way. The alumni reflect on practical experiences and write them down selectively. In the form of work assignments, reflection is directed to specific parts of nursing practice already learned in theory. In this way, alumni improve the transfer of knowledge learned in theory into practice.

courses.title: Introduction to scientific work
courses.module: Theoretical and scientific foundation of nursing
courses.content: Basics of scientific work: excerpting, rules of citation, structure of scientific work, types of citable literature, presentation of the handbook for scientific work of the study program and exercises for handling
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni know the basics of scientific work and apply them. They distinguish between citable and non-citable literature. They know the handbook for scientific work of the study program and apply these in all written texts to be written. They know the term "grey literature" and how to deal with it.

courses.title: Microbiology and hygiene
courses.content: Basic concepts (bacteriology, virology, mycology) and tasks of infection hygiene, environmental hygiene, and epidemiology, immunology and immunoprophylaxis. Infection prevention measures - prophylaxis, vaccination/immunization, disinfection/sterilization. Nosocomial infections and hospital hygiene including applied hygiene in the fields of work of health care and nursing. Infectious diseases (pathophysiology, causes, course of disease, prognosis, diagnostics, therapy).
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni know microorganisms that influence human health. They describe their occurrence, reproduction and resistance. They know the transmission routes and hazards in different settings, recognize persons particularly at risk from infections and set and justify measures for the prevention (e.g. hygiene standards, vaccination schedules, etc.) and control of communicable diseases. They know the pathophysiology of infectious diseases. They differentiate causes of disease and assume the nursing tasks associated with infections.

courses.title: Pathology 1
courses.content: Fundamentals of biology, anatomy and physiology of the human body. Structure and function of cells, tissues and organs. Diseases of kidneys, urinary tract, heart, respiratory organs (anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, causes, course of disease, prognosis, diagnosis, therapy). Fundamentals of pharmacology. Fundamentals of pediatrics: Neonatal including adaptation, complications of pediatric diseases, pediatric emergencies, pediatric fractures, ...
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni will know the biophysics, biochemistry, and biology of the human body. The alumni know the anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology of the following organs and associated structures in the body: kidney and urinary tract, heart and circulatory system, respiratory organs. They explain the corresponding clinical pictures, describe and distinguish their courses and possible complications, as well as recognize symptoms that are relevant for nursing care and include them in the nursing plan in individual cases in the sense of the best possible care of the patients. They know age group-specific differences of the individual clinical pictures and describe possible differences in therapy, diagnostics and rehabilitation. They know the examination methods required for the diagnosis of the respective organ-related clinical pictures and classify findings as pathological or non-pathological. They know conservative, rehabilitative and surgical therapy options for the respective clinical pictures.

courses.title: Pedagogy and sociology for nursing professions
courses.content: Basic concepts of pedagogy and sociology; learning theories; social systems, groups and society, role and organization, interaction; instruction and training.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni possess the knowledge of pedagogy and sociology relevant to the practice of the profession. They know role-theoretical and pedagogical approaches and understand their significance in the professional context. They describe illness and stress, as well as coping strategies, from the perspective of the theories of humanities disciplines and name societal influences. They know action strategies in the professional system and offer support to clients of all ages and their environment. They derive pedagogical action guidelines for care in the sense of empowerment. They have the necessary basic knowledge to carry out the tasks of training and guiding alumni, nursing assistants, nursing assistants, members of social care professions and lay people.

courses.title: Pharmacology
courses.content: Principles of pharmacokinetics Pharmaceuticals for the treatment of: - Diseases of the cardiovascular system - Diseases of the kidney and urinary tract - diseases of the respiratory system - infectious diseases
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni describe central processes of pharmacokinetics relevant for nursing. The alumni know the groups of drugs for the treatment of diseases of the cardiovascular system, kidneys and urinary tract, respiratory tract and infectious diseases. They know the effects, interactions and side effects and pass on relevant information to patients during therapy. They observe unwanted side effects and incorporate these into the therapy decision in the interprofessional process.

courses.title: Professional law
courses.content: Health care and nursing law, professional register law Areas of competence, occupational groups, training, professional authorization
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni have special knowledge from the legal matters relevant to their profession, in particular the Health Care and Nursing Act. The alumni apply this knowledge in practice and thus delimit their own area of competence and that of other professional groups (PA/PFA).

courses.title: Psychology for nursing professions
courses.content: Basic concepts and tasks of psychology, meaning and peculiarities of perception, emotions, needs motivations, thoughts and attitudes in sick and disabled people and in their environment, social psychology. Phases of child development from infancy to adulthood, as well as children's conceptions of body and illness.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni possess the knowledge in the field of psychology relevant for the practice of the profession. They explain the importance of perception, emotions, motivation and attitude and relate them to a person's situation in the context of illness or disability. Alumni describe the development and maturation of the individual across the lifespan. They describe illness and distress, as well as coping strategies, from the perspective of psychology, and name societal influences. They know action strategies in the professional system and offer support to clients of all ages and their environment.

courses.title: Team and group processes
courses.content: Group finding process; team development and teamwork; benefits of group work; conflict resolution; feedback; dealing with constructive criticism; student motivation, role in team, team culture.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni describe different phases of the group finding process. They reflect on their behavior in the group. Alumni describe roles, structures, rules, sequence of actions, and time management needed for teamwork. Alumni give and receive feedback. They name the responsibility of the individual for a successful team culture and actively contribute to a good working atmosphere. The alumni know about possibilities of conflict resolution in groups.

courses.title: Acute care 1
courses.content: Presentation of the areas in the acute hospital: normal wards, special areas, outpatient departments; explanation of the range of tasks in the special areas; tour of the facilities and their special areas.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni gain in-depth insight into the areas of an acute care hospital. They are familiar with the tasks of nurses in special areas and gain insight into these.

courses.title: Child and youth care 1
courses.content: Insight into the field of child and adolescent care (areas of responsibility, content, fields of work); practice of child-specific care techniques in preparation for the first internship in the specialty area.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni are familiar with the special areas of responsibility that arise in the field of child and adolescent care. They implement simple nursing techniques that are relevant in child and adolescent care.

courses.title: Extramural care 1
courses.content: Become familiar with the roles of nursing in the extramural setting (home health, community nursing, physician offices, school nurse, family health nurse, primary care...).
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni will know the areas of responsibility in the extramural setting and describe the differences from intramural nursing.

courses.title: Geriatric care 1
courses.content: Insight into the tasks of geriatric long-term care. Concepts, tasks, forms of living Getting to know facilities with special orientations
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni know the areas of responsibility of nursing in inpatient geriatric forms of living. They gain insight into residential and organizational forms.

courses.title: Health counseling and patient education 1
courses.content: Introduction to the subject matter, materials for counseling, health literacy Work areas in which counseling and education take place Exchange with professionals from the field
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni know the fields of activity in which consulting is carried out. They deal with the quality of information materials. They are familiar with the problems associated with the lack of health literacy in various social groups.

courses.title: Psychiatric care 1
courses.content: Insight into the field of psychiatric health care and nursing (areas of responsibility, contents, fields of work, differences to general health care and nursing) Basic skills of psychiatric nursing
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni are familiar with the scope of work in psychiatric health care and nursing. They are prepared for the first contact with people with mental illness. They assume basic nursing tasks in the psychiatric field.

courses.title: Conducting conversations in critical and existential situations
courses.content: Basic structuring and explanatory approaches of emotion psychology; basic principles of affect regulation; empathic stress; professional handling of critical and existential issues (shame, disgust, powerlessness, anger, fear, grief, frustration, power, suffering, guilt, dying, death); dealing with diversity and recognition of the other; possibilities of relief through conversation; (excursus: salutogenic value and meaning orientation).
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni will name and present basic structuring and explanatory approaches of emotion psychology in a structured manner. They describe principles of affect regulation in a differentiated manner and distinguish between positive and negative effects of empathy. They explain how empathic stress phenomena arise and test approaches of consciously engaging with and differentiating from the emotional world of other people. Alumni can reflect on their individual emotional experience in the nursing context and nursing interaction, make sense of it and apply principles of constructive affect regulation for themselves. They assess the feelings and thoughts of others in the context of explanatory approaches of emotional psychology and implement and combine helpful strategies of conversation in dealing with empathic stress as well as critical / existential topics in a situation-specific manner.

courses.title: Culturally sensitive care
courses.content: Culturally sensitive care: definition, target group, central terms, context of origin and basic features of the theory, possible applications, implementation exercises for practice
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni know the concept of culturally sensitive nursing. They reflect on the approach to and handling of care in other cultures and thus respond more efficiently to the needs of patients and clients with migration biographies in their nursing work. They implement aspects of this concept in everyday nursing care in relation to the situation and the individual.

courses.title: Evidence-based Nursing 1
courses.module: Theoretical and scientific foundation of nursing
courses.content: Philosophy of science basics of qualitative and quantitative research. The research process, ethics in research, quality criteria of qualitative and quantitative research, reading English-language publications. Quantitative research: research question, designs, sampling, questionnaire development, data collection, statistical analysis. Qualitative research: research question, designs, sample, development of interview guidelines, interview techniques and observation techniques, analysis of interviews.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni have basic knowledge of the scientific theoretical foundations of nursing science. They describe the difference between general knowledge and scientific knowledge. The alumni independently edit scientific texts in German and English and excerpt relevant information from them. They summarize information from scientific texts and organize them in a logically coherent manner. They are familiar with the basic features of scientific work. They know the elements of a scientific paper and design a written paper on this basis. Alumni understand the basic principles of qualitative and quantitative research and know the essential steps of the research process. Alumni will know the principles of evidence-based practice and the stages of evidence. Alumni will know the quality criteria of qualitative and quantitative research. Alumni will know the ethical guidelines of research. Alumni will know the basic procedures of qualitative and quantitative research. Alumni will know the advantages and disadvantages of different methods of sampling. Alumni will know the procedures for developing questionnaires and interview guides. Alumni will conduct qualitative and quantitative data collection under supervision. Alumni will conduct a simple qualitative data analysis. Alumni will present research findings in a summarized and descriptive manner.

courses.title: Gerontology and gerontopsychiatry
courses.content: Terminology of the field, demographic development, geriatric research and theories, special features of geriatric medicine, common clinical pictures such as dementia, addictive diseases, multimorbidity, suicide in old age, geriatric depression (causes, course of the disease, prognosis, diagnostics, therapy). Introduction to concepts for the care of persons with dementia: Validation, Böhm, Reality Orientation Training (ROT)
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni describe the significance of being old and growing old in society and explain the effects of specific disease-related processes in the care of the elderly and derive measures for nursing care from this. They know the concept of multimorbidity and define the relevance for nursing care. They define gerontopsychiatric clinical pictures (such as suicidal tendency, depression, dementia and addictive disorders) and name the significance of these disorders for nursing care. They apply this knowledge in a nursing context. The alumni know concepts for the care of dementia patients in the approach and implement them in their nursing activities.

courses.title: Health systems and law
courses.content: Health and social care institutions (hospital plans, independent outpatient clinics, homes for the disabled, homes for the elderly and nursing homes, mobile facilities, inpatient care and inpatient rehabilitation facilities, pharmacies, etc.) Health care authorities (BMGFJ, provincial government, health administration control, Federal Health Agency, Provincial Health Fund). Agreement (acc. to Art. 15a B-VG) on the organization and financing of the health care system, objectives, funding agencies and measures in health care policy. Comparison of selected health care systems (organizational structure of the health care system, health care finances and expenditures, health care provision, service provision, developments and upcoming issues, reform initiatives). Statistical data on health in member states of the European Region - selected country profiles (demographic data, population profile, vulnerable populations, burden of disease, life expectancy, mortality data, hospital morbidity). Discussion of the World Health Report. Individual-based view of care versus population-based view. Current legal basis (laws, regulations). Relevant professional laws in health care. Medical law, medical police regulations, social law (social and health insurance, nursing allowance), patient and human rights, medical device law, labor law, home stay law; health reform law. Basics for the independent practice of the profession.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni are familiar with the institutions of the health and social care system in Austria and have knowledge of the various professional groups in the health care system. They name goals, carriers and measures of the Austrian health policy and describe health systems in selected European country profiles. The alumni recognize the need for information, the problems, the resources and the need for action in relation to the need for care and health and social care and show possible solutions from the perspective of health and nursing. Alumni are familiar with all legal principles in the health care system relevant to health care and nursing. The alumni align their professional actions with the legal framework. They know legally relevant regulations in connection with diagnostics, therapy and medical devices and derive recommendations for action in practice. They have knowledge of the regulations for independent professional practice.

courses.title: Internship and Skills Lab 2
courses.content: Communication with team members, patients, clients, residents, relatives, other professionals. Skills of basic nursing care Special nursing activities (depending on the place of practice) Knowledge and coordination of procedures Relevant medical, pharmacological, dietary knowledge Relevant nursing concepts Skills and simulation training
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni practice and reflect on patient situations and skills in simulations and skills training. The alumni integrate themselves into a nursing team. They communicate appropriately with colleagues, clients, patients, residents and relatives. The alumni perform basic nursing activities in the nursing core competence and in the competence in medical diagnostics and therapy under supervision and guidance. They are aware of the responsibilities involved in performing tasks and know the limits of their scope of practice. They document nursing procedures performed in an appropriate manner. They know the procedure in the practice area and organize it in a meaningful way. The alumni reflect on practical experiences and write them down selectively. In the form of work assignments, reflection is directed to specific parts of nursing practice already learned in theory. In this way, alumni improve the transfer of knowledge learned in theory into practice.

courses.title: Kinesthetics
courses.content: Procedure of the kinesthetic learning model; definition of the terms proximity and distance, concept system, application of the individual concepts, evaluation of movement behavior
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni explain the process of the kinesthetic learning model and move according to the learning model during each activity. The alumni define the terms proximity and distance for themselves and reflect on their handling of them. They name the concept system and list the individual concepts. The alumni work out selected activities from everyday nursing care on the basis of the kinaesthetic concepts and find solutions. They evaluate their own movement behavior and discover the role of their own movement in health and learning processes.

courses.title: Nursing concepts for professional practice 1
courses.content: Seminars on for example: Validation, Böhm, complementary nursing methods, basal stimulation, breastfeeding, kinesthetic infant handling, NIDCAP, conversation in psychiatry, nursing conversation groups for mentally ill patients, clinical assessment, methods of health education, setting-based approaches in community and family health nursing
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni gain insight into new developments in nursing concepts for professional practice. They deepen their specialist knowledge and implement what they have learned in the context of nursing care for and with patients. Alumni choose one concept per semester from the concepts offered.

courses.title: Nursing models and theories
courses.module: Theoretical and scientific foundation of nursing
courses.content: Historical development of models and theories in Anglo-American and German-speaking countries; definition of metatheories, grand theories, middle range theories, situation-specific theory, concept and model; metaparadigms of theories and models, classification of models, application of models and theories in practice and relation to professionalization; nursing models according to Roper, Orem, Krohwinkel, Peplau, Leininger and others.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni know different nursing models and describe their relevance for practice. They name the key terms of nursing and locate them in the individual theories. They distinguish nursing science from other scientific disciplines. They know the terminology of theory formation (grand theory, middle range theory, situation-specific theory, models and concepts). They justify areas of application of different theories and select a suitable theory for themselves as a template for nursing action. They have the knowledge to check theories used in guiding principles for practicability.

courses.title: Nursing process
courses.content: The nursing process as a cybernetic control loop, nursing theories and the nursing process, recognizing and formulating nursing goals; nursing interventions in the context of nursing goals and nursing diagnoses; evaluation of nursing results.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni have basic knowledge of the nursing process and document nursing activities performed. They know the importance of the theoretical models for structuring the nursing process. Alumni know and understand the steps of the nursing process. They create simple nursing care plans with relevant goals and individual interventions.

courses.title: Pathology 2
courses.content: Diseases of the digestive tract, liver and gallbladder (anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, causes, course of disease, prognosis, diagnosis, therapy). Rheumatic diseases and metabolic diseases (anatomy, physiology, patho-physiology, causes, course of disease, prognosis, diagnostics, therapy). Pregnancy, childbirth and puerperium including complications, the healthy newborn, diseases and disorders of the female and male genital system and breast. Models explaining the development of psychosomatic and psychiatric diseases; causes, symptomatology, diagnosis, prognosis, therapy and rehabilitation of psychosomatic and psychiatric diseases.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni will know the anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology of the following organs and associated structures in the body: digestive tract, liver and gallbladder. They know the anatomical, physiological and pathophysiological basis of rheumatic diseases and metabolic diseases. They name basics and explanatory patterns as well as the social and societal relevance of psychiatric diseases. They explain the corresponding clinical pictures, describe their courses and possible complications and distinguish symptomatology relevant for nursing care and include these in the nursing plan in the sense of the best possible care for the patient. They know the examination methods required for the diagnosis of the respective organ-related clinical pictures and classify findings as pathological or non-pathological. They know both conservative and rehabilitative as well as surgical therapy possibilities of the respective clinical pictures. They assign therapeutic measures to the respective clinical pictures and know relevant groups of medications, their effects, interactions and side effects. They use the medical, pharmacological and dietary knowledge for the work area in health care and nursing. They know age group-specific differences of the individual clinical pictures and describe possible differences in therapy, diagnostics and rehabilitation. The alumni know the physiological processes during birth and name complications. They know clinical pictures of the male and female genital organs. The alumni use this knowledge for health care and nursing.

courses.title: Reflection on the interaction between student and client
courses.content: Reflection on practical experiences, relationship between student and client, Hildegard Peplau's interaction model: relationship phases in nursing, roles of a nurse in practice, significance of Peplau's theory in practice; other interaction models (e.g. by Ida Jean Orlando), adherence.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni reflect on previous experiences from nursing practice and relate these to their first practical experiences during their studies. They reflect on the first encounters with clients and their environment during the practical days. The alumni describe the interaction model of Hildegard Peplau, Ida Jean Orlando in its basic features and apply it to an experienced interaction. They recognize the relevance of Peplau's theory to practice. Alumni recognize the complexity of human interaction and possible disruptions. They establish, maintain and resolve social relationships in a professional context in a conscious and reflective manner. They make records of the experiences they have had.

courses.title: Statistics 1
courses.module: Theoretical and scientific foundation of nursing
courses.content: Basics of descriptive statistics: terminology, frequencies, scale level, distribution forms, key figures of statistical distributions (central measures, dispersion measures, shape measures), key figures of statistical correlation (measures of correlation, simple linear regression and related measures), selected graphical forms of representation (univariate, bivariate, multivariate); basics of clinical key figures: Prevalence, incidence, absolute and relative risk change, number needed to treat, odds ratio; basics of diagnostic ratios: Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive value.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni will explain the basic terms and concepts of univariate and bivariate descriptive statistics as well as clinical and diagnostic ratios. Alumni will interpret the results of descriptive statistics and clinical and diagnostic ratios in the context of scientific publications and evaluate them in principle for correct implementation.

courses.title: Basics of health education, promotion and prevention
courses.module: Fundamentals of health and health promotion
courses.content: Models of health promotion; approaches to disease prevention; relevance in practice; public health and the development of health promotion and prevention, the Ottawa Charter as a content-related and methodological integration model of health promotion; exemplary fields of action of health education, health promotion and prevention (e.g. chronic diseases, existential experiences in life such as becoming parents, loss); from health education to health promotion, self-experience of health-promoting behavior, personal health prophylaxis.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni distinguish between resource-promoting and risk-reducing approaches in health education and health education. They will explain selected strategies and methods of salutogenic health education and actively apply them to health education measures in their field of work. The alumni distinguish between health-promoting and disease-preventing strategies in the health sciences (public health). They explain integration approaches to this and use these for the implementation of health education measures in their own professional field. The alumni explain different health theories and models, concepts of health promotion and prevention as well as the holistic health concept of salutogenesis, and present the significance of their own attitudes towards health and their own health actions and critically evaluate these with regard to their field of work. Alumni summarize essential aspects of intervention theory (management cycle, principles) and apply them in situations of professional practice. Alumni identify the central core elements of health-promoting and disease-preventing measures and integrate these into quality-assured health promotion and prevention. They co-develop health-promoting and disease-preventive measures in their field of work on the basis of quality-assured programs and critically evaluate them.

courses.title: Care of people with disabilities
courses.module: Setting- and role-related tasks in nursing care
courses.content: Disability in all stages of life: Definitions, causes and groups of persons at risk, phenomena and experience, care process, curative education and curative education approaches for affected persons and caregivers, interprofessional collaboration.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni are aware of the problems faced by disabled persons specifically in the hospital setting. They apply strategies to improve the situation. They know settings in which persons with disabilities live and assume nursing tasks in these settings. They reflect on the roles of all persons involved in the care of persons with disabilities and explain the resulting problems and integrate approaches for support into their own nursing actions. They are familiar with curative education and curative education approaches.

courses.title: Client and relatives counseling
courses.module: Fundamentals of health and health promotion
courses.content: Basics of counseling, fields of counseling, counseling activities, counseling concepts in nursing, family and patient* education counseling process, selected training programs. Deepening of specific communication skills through interaction exercises and role plays, as well as practical application of individual counseling and informational interview techniques, development of a micro-training concept.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni distinguish between the three approaches of nursing-related patient and family education - informing, training, counseling. They possess theoretical background knowledge for patient and family education as well as basic pedagogical competence. The alumni build up a basis of trust in the educational setting with people of all ages and families in order to promote concordance. Alumni apply nursing-related educational activities in their own responsible area of practice. Alumni describe sources of information gathering and nursing-related education programs. The alumni know strategies and methods of nursing-related patient and family education and design the educational process in a problem- and resource-oriented way. They take an active role in problem and conflict analysis. The alumni possess knowledge of counseling assessment in order to be able to assess the need for counseling in a differentiated manner. The alumni plan micro-trainings according to pedagogical-didactical principles, carry them out and evaluate them, thereby proceeding in an addressee-oriented manner.

courses.title: Deescalation management
courses.content: Coercive measures and violence: definitions, causes, vulnerable group, phenomena in victims of violence, observation and assessment of traumatization, care process and special reporting (mandatory reporting), protective measures for victims and interprofessional cooperation (de-escalation training).
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni deal with the topics of coercive measures and violence, describe problem situations in the care sector and know possible approaches to solving them. They apply de-escalating measures in the care setting.

courses.title: Evidence-based Nursing 2
courses.content: Recognition of a research problem, formulation of research questions, systematic literature research in scientific databases, reading and understanding of research reports in German and English, reviews, description of qualitative and quantitative studies, summary of results of qualitative studies.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni summarize the state of research on a self-selected research problem and derive new questions from it. The alumni conduct a literature search in databases relevant to nursing science. The alumni know the basic criteria for the evaluation of research papers and apply them. They correctly assign research results to the respective level of evidence. They classify qualitative research results on the basis of the recognized quality criteria. Alumni explain the basics of descriptive statistics. They evaluate results of descriptive and inferential statistics in principle.

courses.title: Internship and Skills Lab 3
courses.content: Communication with team members, patients, clients, residents, family members, other professionals. Basic nursing skills Special nursing activities (depending on the practice site) Knowledge and coordination of procedures Relevant medical, pharmacological, dietary knowledge Relevant nursing concepts Health promotion and prevention, patient/client/resident counseling and education Nursing process Skills and simulation training
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni train and reflect on patient situations and skills in simulations and skills training. The alumni integrate themselves into a nursing team. They communicate appropriately with colleagues, clients, patients and relatives. The alumni carry out nursing activities and complex nursing techniques under their own and shared responsibility under supervision and guidance. They are aware of their responsibility when taking on tasks and know the limits of their area of activity. They document care measures carried out in an appropriate manner. They know the process in the practice area and contribute to it in a meaningful way. The alumni apply care concepts learned in theory in practice. They apply the models of counseling and education learned in the field of health promotion and prevention in their work and reflect on these approaches. They use this knowledge to improve the nursing process in order to provide the best possible patient/client/resident care. The alumni take responsibility for procedures and carry out parts of the nursing process under guidance and supervision. The almuni reflect on their practical experiences and write them down selectively. In the form of work assignments, reflection is directed towards specific parts of nursing practice that have already been learned in theory. In this way, graduates improve the transfer of knowledge learned in theory into practice. In self-study, graduates acquire or deepen their knowledge of the clinical pictures relevant to nursing practice (anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, causes, course of disease, prognosis, diagnostics, therapy). The alumni consolidate the skills and abilities acquired in practical courses 1 & 2 and take on increasingly complex tasks.

courses.title: Nursing Diagnostics
courses.content: Nursing history, nursing diagnostics, classification systems, assessment instruments, nursing planning, case understanding, understanding nursing diagnostics, patient autonomy vs. standardized nursing care; subjective meaning of illness, autonomy & adherence.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni carry out the nursing process and justify their nursing decisions on the basis of currently available nursing knowledge. The alumni take a nursing history and determine relevant nursing diagnoses on the basis of it. They know the process of diagnosis and are proficient in the use of current classification systems and assessment instruments. On the basis of an anamnesis, they create a nursing care plan with relevant goals and individual interventions and evaluate it. They base their planning on the criteria of effectiveness (evidence-based practice), well-being, safety, economic efficiency and ecology. In doing so, alumni assess general rules of action in terms of their relevance to the individual case, and relate interventions to the individual needs of their clients.

courses.title: Nursing Ethics
courses.content: Different types of ethics: normative ethics, descriptive ethics, deontological ethics, teleological ethics, discourse ethics, virtue theory, nursing ethics. Processing based on experiences from nursing practice: ethical problems and dilemmas; application of ethical principles - such as dignity, autonomy, responsibility, care, justice, dia-logue - to ethical conflict situations, ethical argumentation and decision-making with the help of theories and decision-making models; professional code of conduct.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni define terms such as morality, ethics, norm and laws. Alumni distinguish between different types of ethics. Alumni are familiar with common ethical problems in the professional context. They recognize ethical conflicts in the professional field of activity. Alumni reflect on ethical conflict situations from practice using ethical principles such as dignity, autonomy and responsibility; they apply theories for decision-making. In dilemma situations, they are able to reach or contribute to an ethical decision-making process in the nursing team or multi-professional team.

courses.title: Nursing concepts for professional practice 2
courses.module: Setting- and role-related tasks in nursing care
courses.content: Seminars on for example: Validation, Böhm, complementary nursing methods, basal stimulation, breastfeeding, Kiaesthetic Infant Handling, NIDCAP, conversation in psychiatry, nursing conversation groups for mentally ill patients, clinical assessment, methods of health education, setting-related approaches in community and family health nursing
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni gain insight into new developments in nursing concepts for professional practice. They deepen their specialist knowledge and implement what they have learned in the context of nursing care for and with patients. Alumni choose one concept per semester from the concepts offered.

courses.title: Palliative Care
courses.module: Setting- and role-related tasks in nursing care
courses.content: Individual, socio-cultural attitudes and attitudes towards life, suffering, farewell, dying and death, coping strategies, definition of palliative care and hospice care, quality of life and patient orientation, requirements for caregivers, mourning process and mourning work, psychosocial maturation process, psychosocial care of patients and their care system, support and comfort for patients, Symbolic language of people in the terminal phase, educational work, pain management, active, passive and indirect euthanasia, patient's will, symptom control and symptom management, pain (development, processing, perception), integration and guidance of relatives, care of the deceased, care in crisis situations, children's ideas about death and dying.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni deal with the phenomena of parting, dying, pain, mourning in different religious and socio-cultural contexts and their coping mechanisms and derive an understanding of care. They justify the requirement profile of palliative care. They develop sensitivity in communication, in dealing with seriously ill and dying people and their reference systems and identify nursing-relevant problems in the nursing process. They take over the care of affected persons and their relatives in crisis situations and, if necessary, involve other professional groups. They describe the development, perception and processing of pain and apply nursing measures within the framework of pain management.

courses.title: Pathology 3
courses.content: Diseases of: - central and peripheral nervous system (anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, causes, course of disease, prognosis, diagnostics, therapy) - endocrine system (anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, causes, course of disease, prognosis, diagnosis, therapy) -pancreas (anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, causes, course of disease, prognosis, diagnostics, therapy) - Hematological system (anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, causes, course of disease, prognosis, diagnostics, therapy) diseases of eyes, throat, nose, ears and skin (anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, causes, course of disease, prognosis, diagnostics, therapy)
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni know the anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology of the following organs and structures in the body: endocrine system, hematological system, eyes, throat, nose, ears, skin, central and peripheral nervous system. They know anatomical, physiological and pathophysiological basics of oncological and immunological diseases. They differentiate causes of disease and assign these to disease patterns. They will explain relevant clinical pictures, describe and differentiate between courses of disease and possible complications. They recognize symptoms that are relevant for nursing care and include them in the nursing care plan in individual cases in order to provide the best possible care for the patient. They know the examination methods required for the diagnosis of the respective clinical pictures and classify findings as pathological or non-pathological. They know both conservative and rehabilitative as well as surgical therapy options for the respective clinical pictures. They assign therapeutic measures to the respective clinical pictures and know relevant groups of medications, their effects and side effects. They know age-group-specific differences of the individual clinical pictures and describe possible differences in therapy, diagnostics and rehabilitation. They use the medical, pharmacological and dietary knowledge for the work area in health care and nursing.

courses.title: Professional self care
courses.module: Fundamentals of health and health promotion
courses.content: Self-care - a clarification of terms; self-care in the mirror of interdisciplinary approaches to health promotion; from cognitive to experiential health literacy; self-care and mental health in the workplace; possibilities and limits of caring for oneself in professional and life contexts.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni describe the concept of self-care in its development from antiquity to the present. They apply modern approaches to self-care. They experiment with the possibilities of different self-care approaches, discover their health-promoting potentials and critically question the limits of self-care approaches. Alumni present approaches to self-care and mental health promotion in the workplace and use them for their own health promotion and disease prevention. They assess the importance of experiential health literacy in distinction to cognitive health literacy approaches and implement practical methods of experiential health literacy in their own everyday life and work.

courses.title: Roles of carers in practice
courses.module: Setting- and role-related tasks in nursing care
courses.content: Relationship between roles and relationships; factors influencing roles and relationships; roles in teams; reflecting on own role images; solving relationship problems; crossing boundaries in relation to roles; neglecting the appropriate role. Role of the nurse in different settings (home health care, family-centered care, community nurse,...). ANP (Advances Nursing Practice) and APN (Advanced Practice Nurse), nurse assessor, tasks in digital health applications (e.g.: e-consultation).
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni explain the meaning of the terms role and relationship. They reflect on their own role models and describe factors influencing the respective role position. They recognize the causes of relationship problems and know approaches to problem solving. They build up a relationship of trust with clients of all ages and with families. They recognize the importance of this relationship for compli-ance. Through regular self-reflection, they recognize possible boundary transgressions or the consequences of neglecting the appropriate role. They are aware of their own role in the context of professional development and actively contribute to the further development of the role. The alumni identify the role and requirement profile in extramural nursing and in relation to digital health. They develop respect for the living environment of the clients and include the family as a support system. They know the internationally recognized role profiles of nurses and make the differentiation to the task profiles of nursing in Austria. They describe future role profiles for nurses in Austria.

courses.title: The salutogenesis model and related approaches in health education
courses.module: Fundamentals of health and health promotion
courses.content: The salutogenesis model - a theory of health and the salutogenetic perspective; salutogenic stress coping approaches in distinction to conventional stress models (biological, psychological, social / work environment related); further protective factor approaches in health research; protective factors as health resources; empiricism and critical appraisal of protective factor approaches; subjective theories and concepts of health and disease; perception of health risks and burdens; perception of resources and challenges; facilitating and inhibiting factors on health behavior change (socio-cognitive process model, phases of behavior change); health education in social systems (setting approach); life skills approach (WHO) in health education.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni describe the model of salutogenesis, assess its significance for the approach to health promotion and illustrate the associated change in perspective compared to disease prevention. They transfer the salutogenic perspective to their own everyday work in health care and derive concrete competencies for practical work from it. They will explain other important stress models (biological, psychological, social/work-related), name coping strategies resulting from them and apply concrete implementation tools for salutogenic stress management in health education. Alumni describe further approaches to protective factor research and summarize central protective factors as health resources. They discuss and critically reflect on their individual health behavior in the light of subjective concepts and theories of health. They apply the central findings of important models of health action for the active accompaniment of people in a health education setting.

courses.title: statistics 2
courses.content: Basics of inferential statistics: probability calculation, point and interval estimates (confidence intervals), principle of hypothesis testing, dealing with statistical significance in the context of clinical relevance, introduction to selected basic test procedures of inferential statistics: a) difference testing (t-tests, variance analyses, selected non-parametric procedures), b) correlation testing (simple and multiple, linear and logistic regression), c) survival time analyses (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank test, co-regression).
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni explain the basic terms and concepts of inferential statistics as well as selected basic statistical test procedures. The alumni interpret the results of these test procedures in the context of scientific publications and evaluate them in principle for correct implementation.

courses.title: Acute care 2
courses.module: Setting- and role-related tasks in nursing care
courses.content: Reflection of the first practical experiences in the field of Nursing care in the surgical area, anesthesia, intensive care units and other areas in the acute care sector
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni will reflect on their experiences in acute care units. Alumni will be familiar with nursing responsibilities in various areas of the acute care hospital.

courses.title: Child and youth care 2
courses.module: Setting- and role-related tasks in nursing care
courses.content: Reflection of the first practical experiences in the field of Deepening of skills in the field of child and adolescent care Care of parents and relatives of sick children
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni reflect on their own experiences in the practical field of child and youth care. They deepen skills for child and adolescent care and apply them in the field. The alumni deal with the care of parents and relatives and know communication patterns for critical situations.

courses.title: Extramural care 2
courses.module: Setting- and role-related tasks in nursing care
courses.content: Examination of the scope of duties of nurses in the extramural sector nationally and internationally. Primary care: interprofessional cooperation, scope of duties of DGKP in primary care
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni describe the areas of responsibility of nurses in the extramural sector in Austria and internationally. They describe the potential of these new fields of activity in relation to population health in Austria. They know the primary care sector, tasks of nursing and potential of this structure in the health care system.

courses.title: Geriatric care 2
courses.module: Setting- and role-related tasks in nursing care
courses.content: Tasks in the intradisciplinary and interprofessional team Areas of responsibility, delegation, quality assurance Work with relatives in the long-term setting
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni describe the area of responsibility of the senior service in health care and nursing in the geriatric setting. They know the basic legal principles of cooperation with the nursing assistance and care professions in inpatient long-term care. They describe the responsibility of the senior health care and nursing service in quality assurance. They describe the tasks of nursing in the work with relatives and apply different interview techniques.

courses.title: Health counseling and patient education 2
courses.module: Setting- and role-related tasks in nursing care
courses.content: Counseling and education - different approaches Approaches to improve health literacy and health literacy. Design of health information
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni know possibilities of patient education and counseling. They know the necessity of counseling in the acute setting and apply counseling tools. They design information materials that help to improve the understanding of health information among different population groups.

courses.title: Psychiatric care 2
courses.module: Setting- and role-related tasks in nursing care
courses.content: Reflection of the first practical experiences, Deepening of skills for the work in the psychiatric field Psychiatry and society (e.g.: discrimination of mentally ill persons), care of relatives (e.g.: co-dependency)
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni reflect on their experiences in practice in the context of the content taught. They apply the skills they have learned in psychiatric care. They explain which social problems arise in the care of mentally ill persons. They know the challenges in connection with the care of mentally ill persons in the family and relatives system.

courses.title: Care of people with specific limitations
courses.content: Changed life situation due to acute and chronic illness: Reflection on the individual and socio-cultural perspective of acute and chronic illness, effects, subjective experience and restrictions in the areas of life; individual care process, support in everyday life management, strategies of psychological hygiene for affected persons and relatives. Case understanding: Definitions, causes, phenomena, vulnerable group and subjective experience of patients/clients with limitations in all areas of life; accompaniment of affected persons during diagnostic and therapeutic measures, primary, secondary and tertiary preventive nursing care, acute interventions and interdisciplinary cooperation, coping with illness for affected persons and relatives. Exemplary case situations, nursing process and handling of medication. Poster preparation, presentation
courses.learningOutcome: Changed life situation due to acute and chronic illness: Reflection on the individual and socio-cultural perspective of acute and chronic illness, effects, subjective experience and restrictions in the areas of life; individual care process, support in everyday life management, strategies of psychological hygiene for affected persons and relatives. Case understanding: Definitions, causes, phenomena, vulnerable group and subjective experience of patients/clients with limitations in all areas of life; accompaniment of affected persons during diagnostic and therapeutic measures, primary, secondary and tertiary preventive nursing care, acute interventions and interdisciplinary cooperation, coping with illness for affected persons and relatives. Exemplary case situations, nursing process and handling of medication. Poster preparation, presentation

courses.title: Evidence-based Nursing 3
courses.content: Definition of a research question, answering of the same within the framework of a literature paper, which is based on a database search and consists of a systematic compilation of results from qualitative or quantitative studies in German and English, their critical appraisal, as well as a conclusion on the internal and external validity of the literature found.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni summarize the state of research on a self-selected research topic and derive a nursing-relevant question from it. The alumni conduct a literature search in databases relevant to nursing science. Alumni systematically summarize and critically evaluate research articles based on defined criteria and correctly assign the research results to the respective level of evidence. Based on the critical appraisal and the interpretation of the results, the alumni answer the self-selected research question and derive recommendations for action for practice.

courses.title: Health Economics
courses.content: Theoretical approaches in health economics, economic position of the health care system in Austria, health care expenditure, gross domestic product and value creation, development of employment, financing of health care services, health care security as an economic problem, performance-oriented hospital financing LKF model 2009, financing of health care services in the extramural sector.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni know the subject area of health economics and know about the financing forms of health services. The alumni define the term health determinants. They know methods of intervention in the health sector. They know biostatistical methods and use results from epidemiological studies for their own field of work. They argue considerations for the further development of health care systems under the aspect of economic efficiency from a nursing point of view.

courses.title: Internship and Skills Lab 4
courses.content: Communication with team members, patients, clients, residents, relatives, other professionals. Skills of basic nursing care Special nursing activities (depending on the place of practice) Knowledge and coordination of procedures Apply relevant medical, pharmacological, dietary knowledge Relevant nursing concepts Health promotion and prevention, patient/client/resident counseling and education Nursing process Practice special nursing techniques Training in the Skills Lab
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni practice and reflect on patient situations and skills in simulations and skills training. The alumni integrate themselves into a nursing team. They communicate appropriately with colleagues, clients, patients and relatives. Alumni perform nursing activities and complex nursing techniques in the competency areas of nursing under supervision and guidance. They are aware of the responsibility when taking over tasks and know the limits of their field of activity. They document nursing activities performed in an appropriate manner. They know the procedure in the practice area and help to shape it in a meaningful way. The alumni reflect on practical experiences and write them down selectively. In the form of work assignments, reflection is directed to specific parts of nursing practice already learned in theory. In this way, alumni improve the transfer of knowledge learned in theory to practice. Alumni apply nursing concepts learned in theory to practice. They use the models of counseling and education learned in the area of health promotion and prevention in the context of their work and reflect on these approaches. They use this knowledge to improve the nursing process in terms of providing the best possible patient/client/resident care. In self-study, the alumni acquire knowledge relevant to nursing practice on the disease patterns relevant to the respective practice site (anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, causes, course of disease, prognosis, diagnostics, therapy) or deepen their knowledge.

courses.title: Nursing concepts for professional practice 3
courses.module: Setting- and role-related tasks in nursing care
courses.content: Seminars on for example: Validation, Böhm, complementary nursing methods, basal stimulation, breastfeeding, Kinaesthetic Infant Handling, NIDCAP, conversation in psychiatry, nursing conversation groups for mentally ill patients, clinical assessment, methods of health education, setting-based approaches in Community and Family Health Nursing
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni gain insight into new developments in nursing concepts for professional practice. They deepen their specialist knowledge and implement what they have learned in the context of nursing care for and with patients. Alumni choose one concept per semester from the concepts offered.

courses.title: Organizational theory and development
courses.content: Related to healthcare organizations: structural and process-oriented organizational forms, organization as a social system (decisions, rules, communication), organizations as cultures, change management - strategies for changing structures, systems, processes, or behaviors in an organization Human resource development (HRD) - areas and goals of HRD, needs assessment.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni name formal structures and the communication relationships and responsibilities they define in organizational units. The alumni name goal-oriented measures for organizational and personnel development and incorporate these into individual career planning. As specialists, alumni are able to help shape and optimize care processes. They assume an innovative key function in the implementation and further development of care processes in the interdisciplinary and multiprofessional professional field of health care. The alumni are aware of the conditions of change management and are involved in the change processes on the wards.

courses.title: Quality and process management
courses.content: Quality dimensions (process, structural, outcome quality), QM systems: ISO, KTQ, TQM and EFQM models, quality management (quality control, quality circles), ÖNORM, DIN, Federal Law on the Quality of Health Services (Federal Law Gazette I No. 179 - patient orientation, transparency, efficiency, effectiveness and patient safety). Process management: strategic process optimization, management of process components, methods and tools of processes, process cost management and evaluation of processes, certification in process management.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni know the quality dimensions and QM systems and take an active role in quality management. The alumni understand the complex networking of planning, control, documentation, automation and evaluation of processes across institutions and professional groups and have detailed knowledge of the structure, content and design of diagnostic and treatment processes. The alumni optimize workflows and process quality at the given interfaces of the respective care and functional areas and initiate the development and implementation of solution strategies in the event of interface problems. They recognize situations relevant to patient safety and act in the best interests of patients. They know reporting systems for dangerous care situations (e.g. CIRS) and assess when these must be used. They know methods to make potentially dangerous procedures safer

courses.title: Selected care techniques
courses.content: Preoperative and postoperative situation of people with planned surgical intervention, effects on the dimensions of life (LD), interprofessional cooperation, preparation and accompaniment in diagnostic measures, special nursing action in food build-up, bladder and bowel activity, mobilization, prophylaxis and pain management, recording in the nursing process; wound management. Hygiene measures, anatomy and physiology knowledge for nursing action, 6 R rule, complications. Exemplary action patterns (preparation, assistance, patient observation and follow-up) for punctures, transfusions, instillations and lavages. Exemplary procedures (preparation, assistance, patient observation and follow-up) for bowel enemas and the placement of urinary catheters, Nursing care of inlets and outlets (e.g. drains, stomas, probes, central venous access).
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni develop sensitivity in dealing with people of all ages who experience a surgical procedure. The alumni describe the pre-, intra- and postoperative situation of patients/clients. They explain the effects on different areas of life. They assist in diagnostic measures and carry out preparatory measures for surgery. They carry out postoperative monitoring and special nursing care. They plan interprofessional cooperation and identify individual problems in the nursing process. The alumni explain action patterns in the care of aseptic and septic wounds as well as stomas, and integrate these after critical examination situation and individual-related into the nursing action. They describe possibilities of drainage systems. The alumni describe the preparation, assistance, patient observation and aftercare of punctures and transfusions. They perform these nursing techniques. The alumni apply the action plan for drains, probes, central venous access, when placing an indwelling bladder catheter, for irrigation or instillations and for enemas. They explain the procedures, reflect on hygiene principles and relevant medical basics.

courses.title: Evidence-based Nursing 4
courses.content: Preparation of a case description of a patient case from practice. In-depth examination of the specialist literature and linkage with the individual situation of the case. Development of a nursing anamnesis, social anamnesis and biographical survey; development of a case-related nursing care plan. Scientific foundation of nursing interventions. Examination of the significance of the disease for the person affected and their environment. Dealing with the question of interdisciplinarity.
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni work out the nursing and nursing-scientific elements of a presented patient case on the basis of concrete questions and present possible solutions for nursing care. They research scientific findings in the national and international field, especially for evidence-based reflection, evaluation and argumentation of health care and nursing. Alumni implement the six steps of the EBN method. They use nursing-relevant and evidence-based nursing scientific knowledge to create norms, standards, guidelines and directives.

courses.title: Internship and Skills Lab 5
courses.content: Communication with team members, patients, clients, residents, family members, other professionals. Basic nursing skills Special nursing activities (depending on the practice site) Knowledge and coordination of procedures Relevant medical, pharmacological, dietary knowledge Relevant nursing concepts Health promotion and prevention, patient/client/resident counseling and education Nursing process Perform complex nursing procedures Skills and simulation training, OSCE examination, interdisciplinary delegation training
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni integrate themselves into a nursing team. They communicate appropriately with colleagues, clients, patients and relatives. The alumni carry out nursing activities and complex nursing techniques in their own and shared responsibility under supervision and guidance. They are aware of their responsibility when taking on tasks and know the limits of their field of activity. They document nursing measures carried out in an appropriate manner. They are familiar with the procedure in the practice area and help to shape it in a meaningful way. The alumni apply nursing concepts learned in theory in practice. They use the models of counseling and education learned in the area of health promotion and prevention in the context of their work and reflect on these approaches. They use this knowledge to improve the nursing process in terms of providing the best possible patient/client/resident care. Alumni take responsibility for procedures and carry out parts of the nursing process under guidance and supervision. Alumni reflect on practical experiences and write them down selectively. In the form of work assignments, reflection is directed to specific parts of nursing practice already learned in theory. In this way, alumni improve the transfer of knowledge learned in theory into practice. In self-study, the alumni acquire knowledge relevant to nursing practice on the disease patterns relevant to the respective practice site (anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, causes, course of disease, prognosis, diagnostics, therapy) or deepen their knowledge. Alumni consolidate the skills and abilities learned in practical courses 1 - 4 and take on increasingly complex activities. They perform the nursing process independently. Under supervision and guidance, alumni assume responsibility for a patient/client/resident or a group of persons in need of care. They become familiar with the responsibilities of ward management.

courses.title: Accompanying seminar and bachelor thesis
courses.content: Determination and processing of a research question relevant to nursing, conducting a systematized literature search, description and critical appraisal of scientific articles, answering the research question posed at the outset and its significance for practice. Supervision during the preparation of the bachelor thesis in small groups as well as through individual supervision discussions on the chosen topic. Discussion of the work steps in the small group setting.
courses.learningOutcome: In the context of their Bachelor's thesis, alumni present what evidence is available as a basis for nursing action for a selected problem. To do this, they research the relevant databases, subject the research articles found to a scientifically sound assessment, systematically summarize the results of their research and make a recommendation for action for practice.

courses.title: Bachelor examination
courses.content: Bachelor examination

courses.title: Internship and Skills Lab 6
courses.content: Communication with team members, patients, clients, residents, family members, other professionals. Basic nursing skills Special nursing activities (depending on the practice site) Knowledge and coordination of procedures Apply relevant medical, pharmacological, dietary knowledge Relevant nursing concepts Health promotion and prevention, patient/client/resident counseling and education Nursing process Perform complex nursing procedures Care and case management
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni integrate themselves into a nursing team. They communicate appropriately with colleagues, clients, patients and relatives. The alumni carry out basic nursing activities in their own and shared responsibility under supervision and guidance. They are aware of the responsibility when taking over tasks and know the limits of their field of activity. They document nursing measures carried out in an appropriate manner. They are familiar with the procedure in the practice area and help to shape it in a meaningful way. The alumni reflect on practical experiences and write them down selectively. In the form of work assignments, reflection is directed to specific parts of nursing practice already learned in theory. In this way, alumni improve the transfer of knowledge learned in theory to practice. In self-study, the alumni acquire knowledge relevant to nursing practice on the disease patterns relevant at the respective practice site (anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, causes, course of disease, prognosis, diagnostics, therapy) or deepen their knowledge.

courses.title: Interprofessional casework
courses.content: Presentation of the meaning and purpose of interprofessional case discussions, presentation of case discussions as a problem-solving approach. Implementation of interprofessional case discussions, joint work with patient cases, reflection on the disciplinary logics of the different professional groups in health and social care.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni recognize and argue the meaning and purpose of interprofessional collaboration in case discussions. In case discussions, alumni identify and argue for practical nursing issues and issues relevant to nursing science in the interprofessional team.

courses.title: Open Window
courses.content: Participation in congresses, conferences or other relevant events relevant to health care and nursing, reflection on experiences, discussion of relevance to the nursing profession. Preparation of a portfolio.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni engage with new trends in the professional field, attend congresses, conferences or relevant events. They reflect on this experience and integrate the knowledge into their professional actions.

courses.title: Practical project
courses.content: Introduction to project management; planning, implementing, presenting, and reflecting on a project relevant to nursing or higher education using mentoring.
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni describe areas of application as well as principles, instruments and methods of project management in outline and implement these according to the project phase for planning, execution, presentation and reflection of simple projects with the help of mentoring.

courses.title: Self-management in the nursing profession
courses.content: Coordination, guidance, training and counseling of patients, other health care professionals and lay caregivers. Self-reflection; principle, goals and tasks of supervision and intervision; concept of "helpless helper"; possibilities to compensate for the daily work routine; teamwork Accident and illness prevention at the workplace Pointing out career paths
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni define physical stress in the work field and develop methods to deal with it. The alumni recognize the necessity of self-reflection. The alumni explain the principle, goals and tasks of supervision and intervision. They describe the term "helpless helper" and observe their own behavior and actions in relation to this background and know the possibilities of seeking professional help. The alumni describe possibilities to compensate for the daily work routine. The alumni reflect on team situations and recognize their own responsibility for successful cooperation. The alumni deal with their own (professional) future, design possible career paths taking into account their own skills, knowledge and available resources and reflect on them.

courses.title: Ward and work organization incl. case, care and disease management
courses.content: Working time models, change management, management of wards and departments: Meeting and knowledge management, team development measures; development of standards, guidelines and directives, coordination, instruction, training and consultation of those concerned; instruction and training of other health care professions and lay caregivers. Definition, conceptual and methodological foundations of case management (CM), functions of CM, CM in acute care, in extramural care and in long-term care / rehabilitation; national and international experience reports of case management tasks. Exemplary case situations. Definition and basics of care management. Definition, conceptual and methodological foundations of disease management, function and importance of interdisciplinary care pathways in acute hospital, outpatient, extramural care, rehabilitation and long-term care. Exemplary disease management (e.g. DM type 2).
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni define management tasks of nursing, documentation and data collection, liability issues, evaluation of results of interdisciplinary care pathways. They apply the knowledge and the course of action in case situations, plan interdisciplinary and interprofessional cooperation and develop a solution concept for affected persons as well as relatives. They argue the use of nursing-specific forms of organization and work in the various nursing settings and care areas. Alumni understand the complex interconnectedness of inter-institutional and inter-professional planning, control, documentation, automation and evaluation of processes and have detailed knowledge of the structure, content and design of diagnostic and treatment processes. As professionals, alumni are able to help shape and optimize care processes. They assume the function of a case and care manager. They assume an innovative key function in the implementation and further development of care processes in the interdisciplinary and multiprofessional professional field of health care. The alumni are familiar with the range of activities of ward and area managers. They guide trainees/alumni, nursing assistants and members of social care professions to take over nursing activities or to support basic care and exercise supervision or accompanying control over the implementation of the activities. They assess the delegability of individual nursing interventions and medical orders to authorized persons. They instruct and guide them in the performance of delegated activities. In cooperation with the person being cared for and the lay caregiver, they develop a quality assurance system that enables the timely recognition of circumstances that no longer permit nursing care by lay caregivers.

courses.title: Acute care 3
courses.content: Immersion in a specialty area of acute care nursing Deepening skills for working in the specialty area
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni will know and apply detailed nursing tasks to a specialty area in acute care.

courses.title: Child and youth care 3
courses.content: In-depth study of selected topics in child and adolescent care. Neonatology, child and adolescent psychiatry, ...
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni have an in-depth knowledge building on the contents of the undergraduate education. They know the "Newborn Individualized Developmental Care and Assessment Program" NIDCAP.

courses.title: Extramural care 3
courses.content: Focus on interprofessional collaboration in an extramural work setting
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni are familiar with concepts of interprofessional collaboration and implement them in the field.

courses.title: Geriatric care 3
courses.content: Tasks of the management in the geriatric area Advanced Practice Nurse (APN) and Advanced Nursing Practitioner (ANP) as topics in geriatric nursing. Forms of care and support for the aged and very elderly in the home setting, geriatric psychiatry
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni describe the management tasks in the setting of long-term care. They deal with the topics APN and ANP in the setting and describe task fields and structural conditions in order to be able to fulfill these tasks. They describe the tasks of nursing in gerontological psychiatry and apply special nursing techniques. The alumni know forms of care and support for elderly and very elderly people in the home setting.

courses.title: Health counseling and patient education 3
courses.content: Tasks of care in the communities, legal and financial background, involvement of relevant stakeholders Preparation of consulting topics for groups Exercises on selected topics in care at the community level
courses.learningOutcome: Alumni will know the central issues of counseling in the nursing setting. They recognize the need for counseling in the community setting. They describe the problems in the field and know the legal and financial background. They create concepts for counseling and education at the community level and apply them.

courses.title: Psychiatric care 3
courses.content: In-depth study of selected topics in psychiatric health care and nursing. Forensics, suicide prevention, child and adolescent psychiatry, ...
courses.learningOutcome: The alumni have an in-depth knowledge building on the contents of the undergraduate education. They present these areas. They apply setting-specific nursing concepts.
